scope: Corollary 4.9 (Constant-line loci) of the manuscript “Logarithmic Kodaira dimension and whole-fiber variation” (preprints/Logarithmic-Kodaira-dimension-and-whole-fiber-variation-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 033 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9b1b750b309e5c5a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 41-42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let π : P → B be a smooth projective morphism with connected fibers over a smooth connected complex algebraic variety. Let T ⊆ B be a connected smooth algebraic locus on which the very general fiber D satisfies κ(D) = 0 and h0(D, KD) = 1. If the entire ordinary top Hodge line of the restricted family has constant projective period in a 42 OPENAI flat reference, its geometric generic fiber is birational to a smooth projective variety over C. The conclusion is equivariant for any prescribed finite fiberwise birational group action. More generally, let B → Z be a morphism of smooth connected complex algebraic varieties with geometrically integral generic fiber. If the same fiber and constant-line hypotheses hold on a nonempty smooth open of every very general fiber over Z, then the family over the geometric generic fiber of B → Z is birationally constant over C(Z), with the prescribed finite action. These birational identifications remain valid after algebraically closed extension of their fields of definition.
